chunks: O you who believe, be custodians of justice (and) witnesses for God, even though against yourselves or your parents or your relatives. Whether a man be rich or poor, God is his greater well-wisher than you. So follow not the behests of lust lest you swerve from justice; and if you prevaricate or avoid (giving evidence), God is cognisant of all that you do.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran command regarding justice when it is against oneself or family?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse is foundational for the concept of 'Adl (Divine Justice), emphasizing that impartiality must prevail even over kinship ties (Qaraba) and personal interests, a principle central to the Imamate's role as just arbiters. It warns against 'Hawa' (capricious desire) distorting legal testimony, reinforcing the obligation of Shuhada' (witnesses) to uphold truth regardless of social status, whether rich or poor. This establishes a universal standard of equity where God’s claim supersedes all human biases, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh regarding fair judgment.
